title: fix off-by-one in status abandon cursor lookup

title: Fix command name collision between LSP auto-registration and extension
description:
The vscode-languageclient library auto-registers VS Code commands for each command in the server's executeCommandProvider.commands capability (see node_modules/.../executeCommand.js lines 47-55). The server declares 'badjuju.new' and 'badjuju.refresh' in COMMANDS. The extension manually registers commands of the same name, causing 'command badjuju.new already exists' errors when the extension activates.

The other commands work because the extension uses distinct names (badjuju.status.open, badjuju.describe.open, badjuju.log.open) that don't collide with the server-declared ones (badjuju.status, badjuju.describe, badjuju.log).

Fix: rename the extension's manually-registered commands to badjuju.new.open and badjuju.refresh.open for consistency with the other commands, and update keybindings/contributes.
close_reason: Renamed extension commands to badjuju.new.open and badjuju.refresh.open to avoid collision with LSP client auto-registration of server-declared executeCommandProvider.commands. Build and 36 tests pass.

title: jj command runner module

Methods: status() -> Result<String>, log(revset: &str) -> Result<String>, describe_get() -> Result<String>, describe_set(message: &str) -> Result<()>, new() -> Result<()>. Each method spawns jj with --no-pager and --color=never, captures stdout/stderr, surfaces non-zero exits as a structured JjFailed error with exit_code and stderr fields. Binary path comes from LSP initializationOptions.binaryPath (matching the existing badjuju.binaryPath VS Code setting) falling back to jj on PATH. Add unit tests under #[cfg(test)] exercising success and failure paths using a tempdir-initialized jj repo.

Add tracing + tracing-subscriber (env-filter, stderr output) so RUST_LOG=debug works. Split main.rs into modules: main.rs, server.rs (Backend impl), and lib.rs as appropriate. Add clap, tracing, tracing-subscriber to Cargo.toml.

neovim: :JJStatus fails with 'Server not initialized' on first call
description:
First invocation of any :JJ* command races the LSP handshake. vim.lsp.start returns synchronously as soon as the badjuju process is spawned, but tower-lsp rejects requests with 'Server not initialized' until the initialize/initialized handshake completes. The second :JJStatus succeeds because by then the client is initialized.

Fix: after vim.lsp.start, wait (vim.wait) for client.initialized to become true before returning the client from ensure_client. Wait should have a reasonable timeout (e.g. 2s) and return nil with a notify if the server never initializes.

title: neovim: setup() with binaryPath and defaultLogRevset
description:
Expose the two VS Code settings (badjuju.binaryPath, badjuju.defaultLogRevset — see clients/vscode/package.json contributes.configuration and extension.ts:176-178, 215-221) as a require('badjuju').setup({...}) function. Today the neovim plugin has no configuration surface beyond overriding cmd.

Files: clients/neovim/lua/badjuju/init.lua (extend), clients/neovim/lsp/jujutsu.lua (read from module state).

Scope:
- require('badjuju').setup({ binaryPath = '/abs/path/to/jj', defaultLogRevset = 'trunk()..@' }).
- binaryPath is forwarded as init_options.binaryPath in the LSP config table.
- defaultLogRevset is consumed by :JJLog when called with no argument.
- setup() must be safe to call before vim.lsp.enable('jujutsu'); document the ordering in the README.
- Tests: round-trip — setup({ defaultLogRevset = 'x' }) makes a no-arg :JJLog invoke the server with arguments = {'x'} (stub the LSP request helper).

Depends on: :JJ* user commands ticket.

title: neovim: read-only buffer for status.jj
description:
VS Code enforces a read-only status buffer via a custom URI scheme (clients/vscode/src/extension.ts:29 READONLY_SCHEME / extension.ts:108-128 openServerResult). Neovim doesn't need a custom scheme — buffer-local options suffice — but the behavior should match: users cannot accidentally edit status.jj and :JJRefresh reloads in place rather than opening a new window.

Files: clients/neovim/lua/badjuju/commands.lua (extend the file opener), clients/neovim/ftplugin/jujutsu.lua (extend).

Scope:
- When opening any path ending in /.jj/badjuju/status.jj, set buffer-local modifiable=false, readonly=true. Choose either buftype=acwrite + autoread or a BufReadPost hook — pick the simpler approach.
- On :JJRefresh (and any command that returns a status URI), reload the buffer from disk if it's already open instead of opening a duplicate.

Depends on: :JJ* user commands ticket.

Files: clients/neovim/lua/badjuju/log_shortcut.lua, clients/neovim/ftplugin/jujutsu.lua (extend), clients/neovim/tests/log_shortcut_spec.lua.

Scope:

- <CR> mapping on log.jj: if cursor line matches, send badjuju.log <revset>; otherwise behave as default <CR>.
- After the buffer reloads, restore cursor row/col clamped to the new line count (matches extension.ts:225-251).
- Tests cover regex/parse only against fixtures.

Depends on: :JJ* user commands ticket.

title: Add revset shortcuts to log.jj header
description:
In the log window, show example revsets as comments under the REVSET line so users can quickly pick a common revset. The VS Code extension should let the user place the cursor on one of these example lines and press Enter to apply it as the REVSET and refresh the log.

    Stack:      (immutable_heads()..@)::

Server work:
- Update commands::run_log so the rendered log.jj header includes the REVSET line followed by a small list of example revset shortcuts (formatted as JJ: comment lines so they are stripped from any save path).
- Keep the existing REVSET parsing in on_log_save unchanged; example lines must be comment lines that on_log_save ignores.

Extension work:
- Add a keybinding / command in clients/vscode that, when the user is editing log.jj and presses Enter on a line matching one of the example shortcut formats, replaces the REVSET line with the example's revset value, saves the file, and triggers a refresh.

- Pressing Enter on an example line in VS Code rewrites REVSET to that example's value and refreshes log.jj.
- cargo test passes with no warnings; biome/tsc clean for the extension.

title: TextMate grammar for .jj status files
description: Replace the placeholder jujutsu.tmLanguage.json (currently matches if/while/for/return — completely wrong) with a real grammar scoped to source.jujutsu. Tokenize the elements that appear in .jj status/log output: section headers (STATUS:, WORKING COPY CHANGES:, STACK:, COMMAND REFERENCE:, LOG:, REVSET:), change-id strings (short lowercase letter sequences like ynrzwrot), commit-id hex strings, bookmark names in square brackets, descriptions, (empty) and (no description set) markers, file-status prefix letters at line start (A, M, D, R followed by space), and graph characters (│, ◆, @, │, …). Provide meaningful scope names (keyword.other.section.jujutsu, constant.numeric.change-id.jujutsu, etc.) so standard themes apply colors. Update language-configuration.json to remove the incorrect C-style comment defaults.

title: Regenerate log.jj on save when REVSET header changes
description: The server tracks open documents via text document sync. On textDocument/didSave for log.jj, re-parse the REVSET: header line, re-run jj log -r <new-revset>, and rewrite the file content via workspace/applyEdit. The user edits just the REVSET: line to change the log view; saving triggers the regeneration. If parsing fails (malformed header), return an LSP error notification to the client.

title: Unify VS Code extension into single package
description: The project currently has two separate VS Code extension packages that need to be merged: clients/badjuju/ (language contribution: jujutsu language id, grammar, language-configuration.json) and clients/vscode/ (LSP client code). Merge them into a single extension at clients/vscode/. Move syntaxes/ and language-configuration.json from clients/badjuju/ into clients/vscode/. Merge the contributes.languages and contributes.grammars entries into clients/vscode/package.json. Delete clients/badjuju/. Add a working main field pointing to the compiled extension output, add activationEvents, and add a TypeScript/esbuild build step with build/watch/vscode:prepublish scripts. Fix the empty scopeName in the grammar (must be source.jujutsu, not empty string).

title: Repo cleanup and project metadata
description: Clean up stale scaffolding in the bad-juju monorepo. Delete the empty root-level vscode/ directory. Replace the incorrect Makefile (currently references dotnet csharpier). Fill out CLAUDE.md Build & Test, Architecture Overview, and Conventions sections with real content. Expand README.adoc beyond its current 3-line stub. Add clients/vscode/out/ and clients/vscode/dist/ to .gitignore. Add server to pnpm-workspace.yaml (currently missing despite being in root package.json workspaces).
close_reason: Deleted empty vscode/ dir, replaced dotnet Makefile with biome+cargo fmt/build/test, filled CLAUDE.md sections, expanded README.adoc, added vscode out/dist to .gitignore, added server to pnpm-workspace.yaml

title: neovim: README docs for tree-sitter parser install
description:
Document tree-sitter parser installation in clients/neovim/README.md so users can get syntax highlighting working.

Scope (focused on tree-sitter only — bad-juju-9zc covers the broader README parity sweep):
- Add a 'Syntax highlighting (tree-sitter)' section.
- Document install via :TSInstall jujutsu (once the parser is published — link to the follow-up ticket).
- Document the in-repo development path: an nvim-treesitter custom-parser snippet that points at clients/neovim/tree-sitter-jujutsu/ so users who haven't waited for publication can still get highlighting.
- Note that highlight queries (highlights.scm) ship inside the bad-juju plugin runtime path — users do NOT need to copy or symlink them manually.
- Cross-reference the redo command for regenerating parser.c (developers contributing to the grammar).
acceptance_criteria:
- README has a section explaining how to install and verify the parser.
- Snippet copy-pasted into a clean nvim setup successfully highlights a .jujutsu buffer (verified manually before close).
notes: Same file bad-juju-9zc will later overhaul for full parity. Keep this section self-contained so the 9zc rewrite can reorganize without breaking semantics.

title: neovim: highlight queries for jujutsu (highlights.scm) + plenary spec
description:
Map the eight tree-sitter grammar nodes to Neovim highlight capture names so .jujutsu buffers render in the user's colorscheme.

Scope:
- Add clients/neovim/queries/jujutsu/highlights.scm with eight captures:
  - (jj_comment) @comment
  - (section_header header: _ @keyword trailing: _ @string)
  - (file_status) @type
  - (empty_marker) @comment.note
  - (bookmark) @tag
  - (commit_id) @number
  - (change_id) @number
  - (graph_char) @punctuation.special
- File placement at clients/neovim/queries/jujutsu/highlights.scm so Neovim's runtime resolves it via the existing rtp:prepend in tests/minimal_init.lua and the README install instructions.
- Add clients/neovim/tests/treesitter_spec.lua:
  - If vim.treesitter.language.add('jujutsu', { path = … }) using the freshly built parser succeeds, parse a multi-line fixture covering all eight rules, walk captures, and assert each expected capture name appears at the right ranges.
  - If the parser isn't loadable on the current machine (e.g. tree-sitter CLI never run), call pending('parser not built') so CI doesn't false-fail.
acceptance_criteria:
- queries/jujutsu/highlights.scm exists with all eight captures.
- treesitter_spec.lua passes when the parser is built; gracefully pends otherwise.
- 'redo clients/neovim/test' passes.
- Manual: opening a .jujutsu buffer in nvim shows the eight categories colored using the user's colorscheme.
notes: Section header capture syntax assumes the grammar exposes 'header' and 'trailing' as named fields — verify against the grammar tickets before writing the query.

title: neovim tree-sitter: commit_id + change_id + graph_char rules
description:
Add the final three TextMate rules from clients/vscode/syntaxes/jujutsu.tmLanguage.json (lines 41-52) to the tree-sitter grammar.

Scope:
- Add to grammar.js:
  - commit_id — \b[0-9][0-9a-f]{7,39}\b
  - change_id — \b[a-z]{8}\b
  - graph_char — single-char match on [│◆@~…○◉╭╮╯╰├─┤]
- Regenerate src/parser.c and commit it.
- Add test/corpus/{commit_id,change_id,graph_chars}.txt with boundary cases:
  - 7-hex commit id matches; 6-hex does not.
  - Exactly 8 lowercase chars matches as change_id; 9-char string does not.
  - Each graph char is recognized; ordinary punctuation is not.

Note: change_id (8 lowercase letters) overlaps with many ordinary English words. The TextMate grammar accepts both interpretations; the tree-sitter grammar should do the same and let highlight precedence decide. If the corpus reveals ambiguities the parser cannot represent, document them in this ticket's notes before closing.
acceptance_criteria:
- grammar.js contains commit_id, change_id, graph_char rules.
- src/parser.c regenerated and committed.
- 'tree-sitter test' passes the new corpus files including boundary cases.
- 'redo clients/neovim/test' passes.

title: neovim tree-sitter: file_status + empty_marker + bookmark rules
description:
Add the next three TextMate rules from clients/vscode/syntaxes/jujutsu.tmLanguage.json (lines 27-40) to the tree-sitter grammar.

Scope:
- Add to grammar.js:
  - file_status — matches ^[AMDR] (first char is the status token; trailing space delimits but is not part of the node).
  - empty_marker — matches (empty) and (no description set).
  - bookmark — matches \[[^]\n]+\].
- Regenerate src/parser.c and commit it.
- Add test/corpus/{file_status,empty_markers,bookmarks}.txt with positive cases (e.g. 'A path/to/file', '(empty)', '(no description set)', '[main feature/x]') and negative cases (e.g. '[' alone, lowercase status letter, mid-line A).
acceptance_criteria:
- grammar.js contains file_status, empty_marker, bookmark rules.
- src/parser.c regenerated and committed.
- 'tree-sitter test' passes the new corpus files.
- 'redo clients/neovim/test' passes.

title: neovim tree-sitter: jj_comment + section_header rules
description:
Add the first two TextMate rules from clients/vscode/syntaxes/jujutsu.tmLanguage.json (lines 16-26) to the new tree-sitter grammar.

Scope:
- Add to grammar.js:
  - jj_comment — matches ^JJ:.*$
  - section_header — matches ^([A-Z][A-Z ]*):(.*)$, exposing the header and trailing-text portions as named fields so the highlight query can color them separately (mirrors the two TextMate captures).
- Regenerate src/parser.c and commit it.
- Add test/corpus/comments.txt and test/corpus/section_headers.txt with positive and negative cases (JJ: at line start vs. mid-line; uppercase header vs. lowercase non-match; header with no body vs. with revset body).
design: Section header exposes two named fields (header, trailing) so highlights.scm can map them to @keyword and @string separately, matching tmLanguage captures 1 and 2.
acceptance_criteria:
- grammar.js contains jj_comment and section_header rules.
- src/parser.c regenerated and committed.
- 'tree-sitter test' passes the new corpus files.
- 'redo clients/neovim/test' passes.

title: neovim: scaffold tree-sitter-jujutsu/ parser directory
description:
Stand up the tree-sitter parser source tree at clients/neovim/tree-sitter-jujutsu/ so subsequent rule tickets can just edit grammar.js and regenerate.

Scope:
- Create clients/neovim/tree-sitter-jujutsu/ with: grammar.js (source_file root rule matching arbitrary text as placeholder), package.json (tree-sitter parser metadata), .gitignore (node_modules/, build/, *.wasm), README.md (one-paragraph 'this is the parser' note).
- Generate and COMMIT src/parser.c, src/tree_sitter/parser.h, src/grammar.json, src/node-types.json.
- Add clients/neovim/tree-sitter-jujutsu/parser.c.do that runs 'tree-sitter generate' (or skips with a notice if the CLI is absent). Mirror the toolchain-absent pattern from clients/neovim/scripts/test.sh.
- Add clients/neovim/tree-sitter-jujutsu/test.do that runs 'tree-sitter test' when the CLI is on PATH, otherwise skips with a notice.
- Wire clients/neovim/test.do to depend on the new tree-sitter-jujutsu/test.do target (the existing find-based dep list may or may not pick it up; verify and extend if needed).

IMPORTANT: do NOT 'redo-ifchange parser.c' anywhere — redo would treat it as a source file and refuse to build. Users invoke regeneration manually via 'redo clients/neovim/tree-sitter-jujutsu/src/parser.c'.
design: Generated parser.c is checked in to match nvim-treesitter and :TSInstall expectations. parser.c.do exists for developer convenience but is never auto-invoked by the test pipeline.
acceptance_criteria:
- tree-sitter-jujutsu/ directory exists with grammar.js, package.json, .gitignore, README.md, src/parser.c, src/tree_sitter/parser.h committed.
- A test/corpus/smoke.txt corpus case (e.g. empty file => (source_file)) passes when 'tree-sitter test' is run.
- 'redo clients/neovim/test' succeeds with and without tree-sitter CLI installed (skips gracefully when absent, no false failures).
- 'redo clients/neovim/tree-sitter-jujutsu/src/parser.c' regenerates parser.c idempotently (no diff on re-run).

title: neovim: tree-sitter parser and highlight queries for jujutsu
description:
Provide syntax highlighting for .jj files in neovim, matching the eight rules in the VS Code TextMate grammar (clients/vscode/syntaxes/jujutsu.tmLanguage.json). Tree-sitter (user-confirmed) rather than a vim syntax file.

Files: clients/neovim/tree-sitter-jujutsu/ (grammar.js, src/parser.c, src/tree_sitter/parser.h) or a sibling repo, plus clients/neovim/queries/jujutsu/highlights.scm.

Scope (8 rules from tmLanguage):
- JJ: comments → @comment
- Section headers ^[A-Z][A-Z ]*: → @keyword
- File status ^[AMDR] → @type (or @constant.builtin)
- Empty / no-description markers (empty), (no description set) → @comment.note
- Bookmarks [...] → @tag
- Commit IDs (hex 7-40) → @number
- Change IDs (8 lowercase letters) → @number
- Graph characters │◆@~…○◉╭╮╯╰├─┤ → @punctuation.special

README to document install via :TSInstall jujutsu or by cloning the parser repo. If the parser lives in a sibling repo, file a follow-up to publish it. Largest single ticket; may be split into 'grammar' and 'queries' subtickets during implementation. Tests via tree-sitter's corpus format in tree-sitter-jujutsu/test/corpus/.

Independent — no deps on other neovim tickets.

title: CI workflow for Rust and TypeScript
description: Add a CI configuration (GitHub Actions workflow at .github/workflows/ci.yml, or equivalent for the local-only git setup) that runs in parallel: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -- -D warnings, cargo nextest run (or cargo test), pnpm install && pnpm -r run build, pnpm biome check . Cache the cargo registry and pnpm store to keep CI fast.

title: Configuration: binaryPath and defaultLogRevset settings
description: Confirm that the existing badjuju.binaryPath VS Code setting flows through to the server via LSP initializationOptions on startup. Add a second setting badjuju.defaultLogRevset (string, default empty meaning use jj's default) that the client passes as an argument when invoking badjuju.log for the first time. Document both settings in clients/vscode/README.md.

title: badjuju.refresh command and status-buffer keybindings
description: Server: implement badjuju.refresh executeCommand. It accepts the active document URI as an argument. If the URI is status.jj, regenerate the status file. If it is log.jj, re-run jj log with the current REVSET: header. Return the file URI after regeneration. Client: register badjuju.refresh (title: 'Bad Juju: Refresh'), bind to keys g and r when a jujutsu-language file is focused. Full status buffer keybindings when the status.jj file is focused: n -> badjuju.new, l -> badjuju.log.open, d -> badjuju.describe.open, g/r -> badjuju.refresh, q -> workbench.action.closeActiveEditor.

title: Align Neovim client with jujutsu language id
description: The Neovim LSP config at clients/neovim/lsp/jujutsu.lua uses filetypes = { 'jj' } but the project standardized on language id jujutsu and extension .jj. Update the config to use filetypes = { 'jujutsu' }. Add a Neovim ftdetect snippet or README so .jj files are recognized as filetype jujutsu. Document the setup steps for Neovim 0.11+ users.

title: neovim tree-sitter: publish parser as sibling repo (follow-up)
description:
Once the in-repo parser is stable and the queries are validated, publish it so end users can install via :TSInstall jujutsu without cloning bad-juju.

Scope:
- Extract clients/neovim/tree-sitter-jujutsu/ to a standalone jennings/tree-sitter-jujutsu repository (history preserved with git subtree split or filter-repo).
- Submit a parser registration PR to nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter.
- After acceptance, update clients/neovim/README.md to lead with ':TSInstall jujutsu' and demote the in-repo path to a developer-only note.
- Consider keeping a symlink or thin pointer in this repo so contributors can still iterate on the grammar without cloning two repos.
acceptance_criteria:
- jennings/tree-sitter-jujutsu repo exists and builds.
- nvim-treesitter PR is merged (or in review with a tracking link in this ticket's notes).
- README recommends :TSInstall jujutsu as the primary install path.
